caseStudy.hook: An in-progress pack of game-ready medieval props built to share one material language — so every asset reads as part of the same world.
brief: Each prop had to work twice: as a hero object that survives close inspection, and as set dressing that reads instantly at gameplay distance.
The pack is built asset-by-asset with a shared kit of metal, wood, leather, and glass treatments, keeping wear logic and value structure consistent across the set.

sections.title: Silhouette first
body: Every asset starts from a clean shape read — ornament is only allowed to accumulate where it doesn't muddy the outline.
The dagger pushes detail density the furthest; the bow holds the opposite end with calm, almost minimal forms. The pack needs both extremes to prove the material kit scales.

sections.title: One material language
body: Metal wear, wood grain, and leather wrap details share masks and grunge logic across assets, so props sit together naturally in a scene.
Texture sets are full PBR — albedo, normal, roughness, metalness, and transmission where the design calls for it — authored in Substance Painter on Blender meshes.

sections.title: Built for realtime
body: Everything in the viewer above renders from the production FBX and texture sets in WebGL — the same files a game engine would ingest.
The inspector exposes wireframe, polycount, and texture resolution per asset, because that's what a technical reviewer actually wants to check.

deliverables: Five game-ready props with full PBR texture sets
Shared material kit (metal / wood / leather / glass treatments)
Realtime WebGL presentation with technical inspector
outcomes: The pack is in active production — more assets land here as they're finished
